chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a man who was on a journey, and with him were a bondwoman of his and two male slave servants. He said to them, “You are both free for the sake of Allah, so bear witness that what is in the womb of this bondwoman of mine is from me.” Then she gave birth to a boy. When they came to the heirs, they denied that and enslaved them. Then later the two male slaves were emancipated, and after they had been emancipated, they testified that their former master had made them witness that what was in the womb of his bondwoman was from him.
He عليه السلام said: “Their testimony is valid for the boy, and the boy for whom they testified cannot enslave them, because they established his lineage.”

key_terms.جَارِيَةٌ: a bondwoman or female slave owned by the man
key_terms.سَفَرٍ: travel or journey during which the event took place
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُمَا: the testimony of the two witnesses
key_terms.ٱلْوَرَثَةِ: the heirs of the deceased man

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of formerly enslaved witnesses accepted to establish a child’s lineage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the admissibility of testimony concerning lineage after emancipation. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that the testimony of the two formerly enslaved men is accepted in favor of the boy’s lineage, and that the boy may not enslave them because their testimony established his descent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5492 - Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad who said:

Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a man who was on a journey with a female slave and two male servant slaves. The man said to the two male slaves, "You both are free for the sake of Allah (swt). Bear witness that what is in the womb of this bondwoman is from me."
Later, the bondwoman gave birth to a boy. When they returned to the man's heirs, the heirs denied the claim and enslaved the boy and the two male servants. Afterward, the two male slaves were emancipated, and after their emancipation, they testified that their former master had made them witness that the child in the womb of the bondwoman was indeed his child.
Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq (as) said: "Their testimony is valid in favor of the boy, and the boy cannot enslave them because they have established his lineage."
